remodeling, furnishing and refurnishing, and equipping and re-equipping school buildings; and equipping, developing and improving playgrounds, driveways, parking areas, and sites?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall Yale Public Schools, St. Clair and Sanilac Counties, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Twenty Million Dollars ($20,000,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, for the purpose of:
remodeling, furnishing and refurnishing, and equipping and re-equipping school buildings; and equipping, developing and improving playgrounds, driveways, parking areas, and sites?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027, under current law, is 1.4 mills ($1.40 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation). The maximum number of years the bonds may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is fourteen (14) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 2.48 mills ($2.48 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).
The school district does not expect to borrow from the State to pay debt service on the bonds. The total amount of qualified bonds currently outstanding is $11,900,000. The total amount of qualified loans currently outstanding is $0.00. The estimated computed millage rate may change based on changes in certain circumstances.
(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote authorizes the sale of $2 million in bonds, repaid through a property tax levy over the life of the bonds.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the borrowing — no bonds are issued and no new debt levy is added.
proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.
proposals.progressiveView: Bonds let communities fund major facility needs — safety, infrastructure, aging buildings — spreading the cost over the years the improvements will be used.

Shall Yale Public Schools, St. Clair and Sanilac Counties, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Twenty Million Dollars ($20,000,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, for the purpose of:
remodeling, furnishing and refurnishing, and equipping and re-equipping school buildings; and equipping, developing and improving playgrounds, driveways, parking areas, and sites?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027, under current law, is 1.4 mills ($1.40 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation). The maximum number of years the bonds may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is fourteen (14) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 2.48 mills ($2.48 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).
The school district does not expect to borrow from the State to pay debt service on the bonds. The total amount of qualified bonds currently outstanding is $11,900,000. The total amount of qualified loans currently outstanding is $0.00. The estimated computed millage rate may change based on changes in certain circumstances.
(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)

proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.

proposals.name: Operating Millage Proposal
proposals.description: Shall Emmett Township’s voted allocated millage of one (1) mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value), as reduced by the required rollback to .6911mils ($.6911 per $1,000 of taxable value), be increased by .3089 mills ($.3089 per $1,000 of taxable value) to restore the millage lost by the application of the Headlee reduction for a period of 20 years, 2026 through 2046, inclusive to provide funds for all Township purposes authorized by law, and may the Township levy such new additional millage…
proposals.ballotLanguage: Shall Emmett Township’s voted allocated millage of one (1) mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value), as reduced by the required rollback to .6911mils ($.6911 per $1,000 of taxable value), be increased by .3089 mills ($.3089 per $1,000 of taxable value) to restore the millage lost by the application of the Headlee reduction for a period of 20 years, 2026 through 2046, inclusive to provide funds for all Township purposes authorized by law, and may the Township levy such new additional millage annually which will raise in the first year of the levy an estimated $108,907.61?
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 1 mill, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.

proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall Yale Public Schools, St. Clair and Sanilac Counties, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Twenty Million Dollars ($20,000,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, for the purpose of:
remodeling, furnishing and refurnishing, and equipping and re-equipping school buildings; and equipping, developing and improving playgrounds, driveways, parking areas, and sites?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027, under current law, is 1.4 mills ($1.40 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation). The maximum number of years the bonds may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is fourteen (14) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 2.48 mills ($2.48 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).
The school district does not expect to borrow from the State to pay debt service on the bonds. The total amount of qualified bonds currently outstanding is $11,900,000. The total amount of qualified loans currently outstanding is $0.00. The estimated computed millage rate may change based on changes in certain circumstances.
(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote authorizes the sale of $2 million in bonds, repaid through a property tax levy over the life of the bonds.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the borrowing — no bonds are issued and no new debt levy is added.
proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.
proposals.progressiveView: Bonds let communities fund major facility needs — safety, infrastructure, aging buildings — spreading the cost over the years the improvements will be used.

proposals.ballotLanguage: Shall the limitation of the total amount of taxes which may be assessed against all real and personal taxable property in the City of Yale, County of St. Clair, State of Michigan, continue to be 2 mills (2 mills which is $2.00 per $1,000.00 of State Taxable Value) of the taxable value of all taxable property in the City, as finally equalized, for each year for 5 years, commencing with 2028 and continuing through 2032, inclusive, for the purpose of providing fire protection services within the City of Yale, including contracted fire suppression, rescue, emergency response, and medical first response services, and related equipment, operations, administration and expenses? The proposed millage is a renewal of the presently authorized millage that expires with the 2027 levy. The city estimates that the millage would generate approximately $96,599 in revenue during the first calendar year it is levied. Revenue from the millage will be collected by the City of Yale and may be disbursed to Brockway Township pursuant to an agreement for fire protection and related emergency response services
proposals.officialTitle: Proposal for Millage Increase for Fire Department Equipment/Operations
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 2 mills for 5 years — generally no increase over what you pay now, plus the restored or added amount described.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.

proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall Yale Public Schools, St. Clair and Sanilac Counties, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Twenty Million Dollars ($20,000,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, for the purpose of:
remodeling, furnishing and refurnishing, and equipping and re-equipping school buildings; and equipping, developing and improving playgrounds, driveways, parking areas, and sites?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027, under current law, is 1.4 mills ($1.40 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation). The maximum number of years the bonds may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is fourteen (14) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 2.48 mills ($2.48 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).
The school district does not expect to borrow from the State to pay debt service on the bonds. The total amount of qualified bonds currently outstanding is $11,900,000. The total amount of qualified loans currently outstanding is $0.00. The estimated computed millage rate may change based on changes in certain circumstances.
(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote authorizes the sale of $2 million in bonds, repaid through a property tax levy over the life of the bonds.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the borrowing — no bonds are issued and no new debt levy is added.
proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.
proposals.progressiveView: Bonds let communities fund major facility needs — safety, infrastructure, aging buildings — spreading the cost over the years the improvements will be used.
